# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
  usage
  exit 1
fi

# --skip: print prompt and exit without running any agent (for post-action testing)
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ "$arg" = "--skip" ]; then
    PROMPT_FILE="${!#}"
    echo "=== --skip mode: printing prompt ==="
    echo ""
    cat "$PROMPT_FILE"
    echo ""
    echo "=== skipped agent execution ==="
    exit 0
  fi
done

# Load dmtools.env if exists (for local runs)
# `while IFS='=' read -r k v; ... export "${k}=${v}"` (matching
# run-teammate-local.sh's loader) instead of `source <(grep ...)`: `source`
# executes each line as a shell command, so any UNQUOTED value containing
# spaces (e.g. `JIRA_EXTRA_FIELDS=Acceptance criteria,Solution,...`) is
# parsed as `KEY=firstword secondword...` — a command invocation, not an
# assignment — which either errors ("command not found") or, worse, silently
# leaves that var (and, depending on shell/error-handling quirks, everything
# defined further down the file) unset. Splitting on the first '=' via `read`
# preserves the rest of the line — spaces included — as one literal value,
# with no shell re-evaluation.
if [ -f "dmtools.env" ]; then
  echo "Loading environment from dmtools.env"
  while IFS='=' read -r k v; do
    [[ "${k}" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]] || continue
    export "${k}=${v}"
  done < <(grep -E '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=' dmtools.env)
fi

# Extract prompt (last argument).
# When cliPrompt is used, DMTools passes the prompt as a temp file path — read it if so.
PROMPT_ARG="${!#}"
PROMPT_SOURCE="inline-argument"

if [ -f "$PROMPT_ARG" ]; then
  PROMPT="$(cat "$PROMPT_ARG")"
  PROMPT_SOURCE="$PROMPT_ARG"
else
  PROMPT="$PROMPT_ARG"
fi

if [ -z "$PROMPT" ]; then
  echo "Error: prompt argument is required" >&2
  usage
  exit 1
fi

PROMPT_BYTES=$(printf "%s" "$PROMPT" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
echo "=== AGENT PROMPT START ==="
echo "Prompt source: ${PROMPT_SOURCE}"
echo "Prompt size: ${PROMPT_BYTES} bytes"
echo ""
printf "%s\n" "$PROMPT"
echo ""
echo "=== AGENT PROMPT END ==="
echo ""

# Extract extra arguments (everything except the last — the prompt)
# These are passed through to the agent to support flags like --continue --resume
PASS_ARGS=()
if [ $# -gt 1 ]; then
  PASS_ARGS=("${@:1:$#-1}")
fi

# Determine provider
PROVIDER="${AI_AGENT_PROVIDER:-cursor}"
echo "AI Agent Provider: $PROVIDER"

# Derive a human-readable usage name for token-report files.
# Prefer the agent config name (e.g. story_acceptance_criteria from CONFIG_FILE),
# then fall back to the workflow-provided AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE,
# and finally fall back to the provider name for standalone/local runs.
AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="${PROVIDER}"
CONFIG_FILE="${CONFIG_FILE:-${AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE:-}}"
if [ -n "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" ]; then
  case "${CONFIG_FILE}" in
    */.dmtools/packs/*)
      # Pack launch surface (Wave 2): the config lives inside an unpacked
      # agent pack (~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<v>/…, e.g. launch.json) —
      # report usage under the AGENT NAME (the pack dir), not the file
      # basename, so token-usage reports stay stable across the migration.
      usage_name="${CONFIG_FILE#*/.dmtools/packs/}"
      usage_name="${usage_name%%/*}"
      usage_name="${usage_name%-[0-9]*}"
      AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="${usage_name:-launch}"
      ;;
    *)
      AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="$(basename "${CONFIG_FILE}" .json)"
      ;;
  esac
fi
export AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME
echo "AI Agent Usage Name: ${AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME}"

# Marker used by rescue_misplaced_outputs() (see providers/_common.sh) to
# detect output files the agent wrote to the wrong directory — e.g. because
# its persistent Bash shell `cd`'d into a dependency checkout while exploring
# source and never returned before writing outputs/*.
RESCUE_MARKER="$(start_output_rescue_marker)"

# ── git push guard (mechanical, dmtools-agents#542) ─────────────────────────
# Interpose a `git` shim at the front of PATH for the WHOLE agent subprocess
# tree: the provider CLI (fa/claude/cursor/…) inherits it, so the LLM agent's
# own shell-tool `git push` is intercepted, and the JS post-actions' pushes
# (via cli_execute_command, PATH-resolved) go through it too. The shim
# refuses pushes to protected branches (main/master/default) and commit
# messages with closing keywords — prompts alone proved insufficient (the
# gh-992 incident: crafted "(closes #992)" commit pushed straight to main).
GIT_GUARD_DIR=""
if [ -f "${SCRIPT_DIR}/git-push-guard.sh" ]; then
  # Do not arm a second shim when one is already on PATH (the factory
  # workflow prepends its own guard dir for the whole step): two copies
  # would resolve each other as "real git" and exec-loop forever
  # (RCA 2026-09-28 legs hang). The shim itself also skips sibling…

But looking at the code, developBugAndCreatePR.js has its own pre-check: if `!hasResponseMd`, it does its own cold reset (comment → Ready For Development → wip removal → throwInterruptedReset) BEFORE delegating to developTicket.action(). So for the bug flow, the response.md-missing branch is in developBugAndCreatePR.js. For the story flow, it's in developTicketAndCreatePR.js (two branches: the "No changes were made" Case B, and the post-gates "response.md missing" branch).

The ticket's architecture says: "C2 — resume-before-cold-reset (`agents/js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js`, shared by the bug and story post-actions via `developBugAndCreatePR.js`)".

Hmm — "shared by the bug and story post-actions via developBugAndCreatePR.js" means: developTicketAndCreatePR.js is the shared module, which developBugAndCreatePR.js (bug post-action) delegates to. So the fix should live in a shared place.

The cleanest approach following the ticket: add a shared helper — e.g. in `feedbackLoop.js` or a new module — `resumeOnceForMissingResponse()` that:
1. Checks if the session is resumable (feedback loop enabled / wrapper invocable).
2. Makes exactly ONE bounded resume attempt: re-invoke `agents/scripts/run-agent.sh` with a follow-up prompt: "the verification run hung: `bash_job stop` it, note it, write `outputs/response.md` and finish".
3. Bounded by a hard cap (recommend ≤40 min; must fit job's remaining timeout budget) — this bounded-ness needs to be implemented via the command itself, e.g. `timeout <seconds> bash agents/scripts/run-agent.sh --continue <promptPath>` — since cli_execute_command is synchronous from the JS side. A hard cap on the wrapper invocation can be enforced with the shell `timeout` command. That's hermetic-testable via mocking cli_execute_command and asserting the command contains the timeout cap.
4. Then re-check response.md.

And integrate into `developTicketAndCreatePR.js` response.md-missing branch(es), so that:
- AC2: missing response.md + resumable → wrapper invoked exactly ONCE with follow-up prompt; zero tracker side effects before outcome resolves.
- AC3: resume writes response.md → normal continuation (PR creation proceeds; NO reset comment, NO status move, run NOT failed).
- AC4: resume fails/times out → existing reset sequence verbatim.
- AC5: non-resumable + missing → cold reset directly (no wrapper invocation).
- AC6: fatal CLI/env class still takes throwFatalCliEnvironmentError (resume never preempts it).

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
  usage
  exit 1
fi

# --skip: print prompt and exit without running any agent (for post-action testing)
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ "$arg" = "--skip" ]; then
    PROMPT_FILE="${!#}"
    echo "=== --skip mode: printing prompt ==="
    echo ""
    cat "$PROMPT_FILE"
    echo ""
    echo "=== skipped agent execution ==="
    exit 0
  fi
done

# Load dmtools.env if exists (for local runs)
# `while IFS='=' read -r k v; ... export "${k}=${v}"` (matching
# run-teammate-local.sh's loader) instead of `source <(grep ...)`: `source`
# executes each line as a shell command, so any UNQUOTED value containing
# spaces (e.g. `JIRA_EXTRA_FIELDS=Acceptance criteria,Solution,...`) is
# parsed as `KEY=firstword secondword...` — a command invocation, not an
# assignment — which either errors ("command not found") or, worse, silently
# leaves that var (and, depending on shell/error-handling quirks, everything
# defined further down the file) unset. Splitting on the first '=' via `read`
# preserves the rest of the line — spaces included — as one literal value,
# with no shell re-evaluation.
if [ -f "dmtools.env" ]; then
  echo "Loading environment from dmtools.env"
  while IFS='=' read -r k v; do
    [[ "${k}" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]] || continue
    export "${k}=${v}"
  done < <(grep -E '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=' dmtools.env)
fi

# Extract prompt (last argument).
# When cliPrompt is used, DMTools passes the prompt as a temp file path — read it if so.
PROMPT_ARG="${!#}"
PROMPT_SOURCE="inline-argument"

if [ -f "$PROMPT_ARG" ]; then
  PROMPT="$(cat "$PROMPT_ARG")"
  PROMPT_SOURCE="$PROMPT_ARG"
else
  PROMPT="$PROMPT_ARG"
fi

if [ -z "$PROMPT" ]; then
  echo "Error: prompt argument is required" >&2
  usage
  exit 1
fi

PROMPT_BYTES=$(printf "%s" "$PROMPT" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
echo "=== AGENT PROMPT START ==="
echo "Prompt source: ${PROMPT_SOURCE}"
echo "Prompt size: ${PROMPT_BYTES} bytes"
echo ""
printf "%s\n" "$PROMPT"
echo ""
echo "=== AGENT PROMPT END ==="
echo ""

# Extract extra arguments (everything except the last — the prompt)
# These are passed through to the agent to support flags like --continue --resume
PASS_ARGS=()
if [ $# -gt 1 ]; then
  PASS_ARGS=("${@:1:$#-1}")
fi

# Determine provider
PROVIDER="${AI_AGENT_PROVIDER:-cursor}"
echo "AI Agent Provider: $PROVIDER"

# Derive a human-readable usage name for token-report files.
# Prefer the agent config name (e.g. story_acceptance_criteria from CONFIG_FILE),
# then fall back to the workflow-provided AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE,
# and finally fall back to the provider name for standalone/local runs.
AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="${PROVIDER}"
CONFIG_FILE="${CONFIG_FILE:-${AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE:-}}"
if [ -n "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" ]; then
  case "${CONFIG_FILE}" in
    */.dmtools/packs/*)
      # Pack launch surface (Wave 2): the config lives inside an unpacked
      # agent pack (~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<v>/…, e.g. launch.json) —
      # report usage under the AGENT NAME (the pack dir), not the file
      # basename, so token-usage reports stay stable across the migration.
      usage_name="${CONFIG_FILE#*/.dmtools/packs/}"
      usage_name="${usage_name%%/*}"
      usage_name="${usage_name%-[0-9]*}"
      AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="${usage_name:-launch}"
      ;;
    *)
      AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="$(basename "${CONFIG_FILE}" .json)"
      ;;
  esac
fi
export AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME
echo "AI Agent Usage Name: ${AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME}"

# Marker used by rescue_misplaced_outputs() (see providers/_common.sh) to
# detect output files the agent wrote to the wrong directory — e.g. because
# its persistent Bash shell `cd`'d into a dependency checkout while exploring
# source and never returned before writing outputs/*.
RESCUE_MARKER="$(start_output_rescue_marker)"

# ── git push guard (mechanical, dmtools-agents#542) ─────────────────────────
# Interpose a `git` shim at the front of PATH for the WHOLE agent subprocess
# tree: the provider CLI (fa/claude/cursor/…) inherits it, so the LLM agent's
# own shell-tool `git push` is intercepted, and the JS post-actions' pushes
# (via cli_execute_command, PATH-resolved) go through it too. The shim
# refuses pushes to protected branches (main/master/default) and commit
# messages with closing keywords — prompts alone proved insufficient (the
# gh-992 incident: crafted "(closes #992)" commit pushed straight to main).
GIT_GUARD_DIR=""
if [ -f "${SCRIPT_DIR}/git-push-guard.sh" ]; then
  # Do not arm a second shim when one is already on PATH (the factory
  # workflow prepends its own guard dir for the whole step): two copies
  # would resolve each other as "real git" and exec-loop forever
  # (RCA 2026-09-28 legs hang). The shim itself also skips sibling…

**Root cause**: 
1. `prompts/bash_tools.md` BGJOBS subgraph (B1–B6) gives no disposal rule for a HUNG background job — the agent has no guidance to stop a hung child and finish the deliverable (gh-1341: the agent parked 20:00–20:04 in a foreground sleep-poll circle, then the run died at the reset).

# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
  usage
  exit 1
fi

# --skip: print prompt and exit without running any agent (for post-action testing)
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ "$arg" = "--skip" ]; then
    PROMPT_FILE="${!#}"
    echo "=== --skip mode: printing prompt ==="
    echo ""
    cat "$PROMPT_FILE"
    echo ""
    echo "=== skipped agent execution ==="
    exit 0
  fi
done

# Load dmtools.env if exists (for local runs)
# `while IFS='=' read -r k v; ... export "${k}=${v}"` (matching
# run-teammate-local.sh's loader) instead of `source <(grep ...)`: `source`
# executes each line as a shell command, so any UNQUOTED value containing
# spaces (e.g. `JIRA_EXTRA_FIELDS=Acceptance criteria,Solution,...`) is
# parsed as `KEY=firstword secondword...` — a command invocation, not an
# assignment — which either errors ("command not found") or, worse, silently
# leaves that var (and, depending on shell/error-handling quirks, everything
# defined further down the file) unset. Splitting on the first '=' via `read`
# preserves the rest of the line — spaces included — as one literal value,
# with no shell re-evaluation.
if [ -f "dmtools.env" ]; then
  echo "Loading environment from dmtools.env"
  while IFS='=' read -r k v; do
    [[ "${k}" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]] || continue
    export "${k}=${v}"
  done < <(grep -E '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=' dmtools.env)
fi

# Extract prompt (last argument).
# When cliPrompt is used, DMTools passes the prompt as a temp file path — read it if so.
PROMPT_ARG="${!#}"
PROMPT_SOURCE="inline-argument"

if [ -f "$PROMPT_ARG" ]; then
  PROMPT="$(cat "$PROMPT_ARG")"
  PROMPT_SOURCE="$PROMPT_ARG"
else
  PROMPT="$PROMPT_ARG"
fi

if [ -z "$PROMPT" ]; then
  echo "Error: prompt argument is required" >&2
  usage
  exit 1
fi

PROMPT_BYTES=$(printf "%s" "$PROMPT" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
echo "=== AGENT PROMPT START ==="
echo "Prompt source: ${PROMPT_SOURCE}"
echo "Prompt size: ${PROMPT_BYTES} bytes"
echo ""
printf "%s\n" "$PROMPT"
echo ""
echo "=== AGENT PROMPT END ==="
echo ""

# Extract extra arguments (everything except the last — the prompt)
# These are passed through to the agent to support flags like --continue --resume
PASS_ARGS=()
if [ $# -gt 1 ]; then
  PASS_ARGS=("${@:1:$#-1}")
fi

# Determine provider
PROVIDER="${AI_AGENT_PROVIDER:-cursor}"
echo "AI Agent Provider: $PROVIDER"

# Derive a human-readable usage name for token-report files.
# Prefer the agent config name (e.g. story_acceptance_criteria from CONFIG_FILE),
# then fall back to the workflow-provided AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE,
# and finally fall back to the provider name for standalone/local runs.
AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="${PROVIDER}"
CONFIG_FILE="${CONFIG_FILE:-${AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE:-}}"
if [ -n "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" ]; then
  case "${CONFIG_FILE}" in
    */.dmtools/packs/*)
      # Pack launch surface (Wave 2): the config lives inside an unpacked
      # agent pack (~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<v>/…, e.g. launch.json) —
      # report usage under the AGENT NAME (the pack dir), not the file
      # basename, so token-usage reports stay stable across the migration.
      usage_name="${CONFIG_FILE#*/.dmtools/packs/}"
      usage_name="${usage_name%%/*}"
      usage_name="${usage_name%-[0-9]*}"
      AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="${usage_name:-launch}"
      ;;
    *)
      AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="$(basename "${CONFIG_FILE}" .json)"
      ;;
  esac
fi
export AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME
echo "AI Agent Usage Name: ${AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME}"

# Marker used by rescue_misplaced_outputs() (see providers/_common.sh) to
# detect output files the agent wrote to the wrong directory — e.g. because
# its persistent Bash shell `cd`'d into a dependency checkout while exploring
# source and never returned before writing outputs/*.
RESCUE_MARKER="$(start_output_rescue_marker)"

# ── git push guard (mechanical, dmtools-agents#542) ─────────────────────────
# Interpose a `git` shim at the front of PATH for the WHOLE agent subprocess
# tree: the provider CLI (fa/claude/cursor/…) inherits it, so the LLM agent's
# own shell-tool `git push` is intercepted, and the JS post-actions' pushes
# (via cli_execute_command, PATH-resolved) go through it too. The shim
# refuses pushes to protected branches (main/master/default) and commit
# messages with closing keywords — prompts alone proved insufficient (the
# gh-992 incident: crafted "(closes #992)" commit pushed straight to main).
GIT_GUARD_DIR=""
if [ -f "${SCRIPT_DIR}/git-push-guard.sh" ]; then
  # Do not arm a second shim when one is already on PATH (the factory
  # workflow prepends its own guard dir for the whole step): two copies
  # would resolve each other as "real git" and exec-loop forever
  # (RCA 2026-09-28 legs hang). The shim itself also skips sibling…

Now let me plan the RCA and implementation.

## RCA

**Bug**: A dev leg that finishes its edits but whose verification (background job) hangs never writes `outputs/response.md`; the dev post-action's missing-response.md branch cold-resets the session (interrupted comment + Ready For Development + wip removal + red run via `throwInterruptedReset`), discarding a finished session's work and forcing a full re-run.

**Root cause**: 
1. `prompts/bash_tools.md` BGJOBS subgraph (B1–B6) gives no disposal rule for a HUNG background job — the agent has no guidance to stop a hung child and finish the deliverable (gh-1341: the agent parked 20:00–20:04 in a foreground sleep-poll circle, then the run died at the reset).
2. `js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js` response.md-missing branch immediately runs the cold-reset sequence — no cheaper recovery (resume of the still-resumable fa session) is attempted first.

**Fix approach**:
- C1: Add node B7 to the BGJOBS subgraph: hung job disposal rule.
- C2: In the missing-response.md branch of `developTicketAndCreatePR.js`, before the cold reset: if the fatal CLI/env class doesn't apply and the session is resumable, make exactly ONE bounded resume attempt via the wrapper (`bash agents/scripts/run-agent.sh --continue <prompt>`), then re-check response.md. If present → continue normal path. If still missing/failed → existing cold-reset sequence verbatim.

Now, design decisions for C2:

1. **Where does the resume logic live?** The ticket says "agents/js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js, shared by the bug and story post-actions via developBugAndCreatePR.js". The story post-action's missing-response branch is in developTicketAndCreatePR.js. The bug post-action has its own earlier missing-response branch in developBugAndCreatePR.js (path 3 pre-check). 

Hmm. Should the bug pre-check branch also get the resume? The ticket's "Capability surface" table says "response.md missing, session resumable → 1 bounded resume". And the test plan says UT-* in test_developTicketAndCreatePR.js. The minimal fix per the ticket targets developTicketAndCreatePR.js. The bug flow's own missing-response branch (in developBugAndCreatePR.js) happens BEFORE delegating... 

Let me think. If a bug dev leg hangs its verification: all edits done, rca.md maybe written, but response.md missing and maybe git changes present. developBugAndCreatePR.action() path 3 pre-check: hasGitChanges=true (rca.md), hasResponseMd=false → pushes partial work → interrupted comment → Ready For Development → removeLabels → throwInterruptedReset. It never delegates to developTicket.action(). So the bug flow wouldn't benefit from a fix only in developTicketAndCreatePR.js.

The ticket says C2 is in developTicketAndCreatePR.js "shared by the bug and story post-actions via developBugAndCreatePR.js". I read this as: the shared resume helper should live in a place used by the dev post-action(s). To honor both flows with minimal duplication, the natural design:

- Add a shared bounded-resume helper — I'll put it in `js/common/feedbackLoop.js` (it already owns resume mechanics: markers, prompts, wrapper invocation) — e.g. `resumeForMissingResponse(options)` or a more general `resumeOnce(options)` with a hard cap.

"C2 — resume-before-cold-reset (`agents/js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js`, shared by the bug and story post-actions via `developBugAndCreatePR.js`). Subject: the dev post-action's response.md-missing branch. New order: 1. response.md missing/blank AND the session is resumable → one resume attempt... 3. Still missing, resume failed / timed out / non-applicable → the EXISTING cold-reset sequence runs verbatim."

So the C2 change: the dev post-action's response.md-missing branch. In the codebase, there are exactly two implementations of that branch:
1. `developBugAndCreatePR.js` (bug post-action pre-check path) — cold reset + throwInterruptedReset.
2. `developTicketAndCreatePR.js` — two sites: "No changes were made" Case B (response.md missing + no git changes) and the post-gates missing-response branch (partial work committed/pushed, response.md missing).

The minimal fix honoring the ticket: implement the resume helper in one place (feedbackLoop.js — it's the shared resume machinery, already required by developTicketAndCreatePR.js) and wire it into the missing-response branch(es) of developTicketAndCreatePR.js, plus the bug pre-check branch in developBugAndCreatePR.js (since the ticket explicitly mentions the bug post-action shares it).

Which flow? "the dev post-action, before cold-resetting a resumable session whose outputs/response.md is missing". The interrupted comment mentioned "partial work was pushed to branch" — the log shows "no response.md → cold reset (interrupted comment + Ready For Development + wip removal + red run via throwInterruptedReset)". Both flows produce that. The gh-742 origin was dmtools-dart gh-350 (story flow).

I.e., "put the logic in developTicketAndCreatePR.js, which is the module shared by both post-actions".

But mechanically, the bug flow's missing-response branch never reaches developTicketAndCreatePR.js... unless I ALSO change developBugAndCreatePR to route through the shared helper. Hmm.

Decision: Put the resume helper in `js/common/feedbackLoop.js` (shared resume machinery, testable in isolation, already the module both flows use for resumeAgent), and wire it into ALL dev-post-action response.md-missing cold-reset sites:

2. `developTicketAndCreatePR.js` post-gates missing-response branch — after the fatal check.
3. `developBugAndCreatePR.js` path-3 pre-check (partial work) — after pushing partial work, before the interrupted comment.

Hmm, wait. Point 3: should the resume happen before or after pushing partial work? If the resume succeeds and writes response.md, then... the flow continues: `developTicket.action(params)` runs, which does git ops (staging + commit + push). If we already pushed partial work, that's fine — the branch is pushed, PR creation proceeds. Actually pushing partial work first is harmless (it becomes part of the PR). But it does side effects (push, wip commit) before the resume outcome resolves... The ordering invariant in the ticket: "the tracker side effects of the existing path (comment, status move, wip removal) fire ONLY after the resume attempt fails" — pushing partial work is not a tracker side effect (it's a git side effect, and it's recovery-preserving). blocks.text:
# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
  usage
  exit 1
fi

# --skip: print prompt and exit without running any agent (for post-action testing)
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ "$arg" = "--skip" ]; then
    PROMPT_FILE="${!#}"
    echo "=== --skip mode: printing prompt ==="
    echo ""
    cat "$PROMPT_FILE"
    echo ""
    echo "=== skipped agent execution ==="
    exit 0
  fi
done

# Load dmtools.env if exists (for local runs)
# `while IFS='=' read -r k v; ... export "${k}=${v}"` (matching
# run-teammate-local.sh's loader) instead of `source <(grep ...)`: `source`
# executes each line as a shell command, so any UNQUOTED value containing
# spaces (e.g. `JIRA_EXTRA_FIELDS=Acceptance criteria,Solution,...`) is
# parsed as `KEY=firstword secondword...` — a command invocation, not an
# assignment — which either errors ("command not found") or, worse, silently
# leaves that var (and, depending on shell/error-handling quirks, everything
# defined further down the file) unset. Splitting on the first '=' via `read`
# preserves the rest of the line — spaces included — as one literal value,
# with no shell re-evaluation.
if [ -f "dmtools.env" ]; then
  echo "Loading environment from dmtools.env"
  while IFS='=' read -r k v; do
    [[ "${k}" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]] || continue
    export "${k}=${v}"
  done < <(grep -E '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=' dmtools.env)
fi

# Extract prompt (last argument).
# When cliPrompt is used, DMTools passes the prompt as a temp file path — read it if so.
PROMPT_ARG="${!#}"
PROMPT_SOURCE="inline-argument"

if [ -f "$PROMPT_ARG" ]; then
  PROMPT="$(cat "$PROMPT_ARG")"
  PROMPT_SOURCE="$PROMPT_ARG"
else
  PROMPT="$PROMPT_ARG"
fi

if [ -z "$PROMPT" ]; then
  echo "Error: prompt argument is required" >&2
  usage
  exit 1
fi

PROMPT_BYTES=$(printf "%s" "$PROMPT" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
echo "=== AGENT PROMPT START ==="
echo "Prompt source: ${PROMPT_SOURCE}"
echo "Prompt size: ${PROMPT_BYTES} bytes"
echo ""
printf "%s\n" "$PROMPT"
echo ""
echo "=== AGENT PROMPT END ==="
echo ""

# Extract extra arguments (everything except the last — the prompt)
# These are passed through to the agent to support flags like --continue --resume
PASS_ARGS=()
if [ $# -gt 1 ]; then
  PASS_ARGS=("${@:1:$#-1}")
fi

# Determine provider
PROVIDER="${AI_AGENT_PROVIDER:-cursor}"
echo "AI Agent Provider: $PROVIDER"

# Derive a human-readable usage name for token-report files.
# Prefer the agent config name (e.g. story_acceptance_criteria from CONFIG_FILE),
# then fall back to the workflow-provided AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE,
# and finally fall back to the provider name for standalone/local runs.
AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="${PROVIDER}"
CONFIG_FILE="${CONFIG_FILE:-${AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE:-}}"
if [ -n "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" ]; then
  case "${CONFIG_FILE}" in
    */.dmtools/packs/*)
      # Pack launch surface (Wave 2): the config lives inside an unpacked
      # agent pack (~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<v>/…, e.g. launch.json) —
      # report usage under the AGENT NAME (the pack dir), not the file
      # basename, so token-usage reports stay stable across the migration.
      usage_name="${CONFIG_FILE#*/.dmtools/packs/}"
      usage_name="${usage_name%%/*}"
      usage_name="${usage_name%-[0-9]*}"
      AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="${usage_name:-launch}"
      ;;
    *)
      AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="$(basename "${CONFIG_FILE}" .json)"
      ;;
  esac
fi
export AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME
echo "AI Agent Usage Name: ${AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME}"

# Marker used by rescue_misplaced_outputs() (see providers/_common.sh) to
# detect output files the agent wrote to the wrong directory — e.g. because
# its persistent Bash shell `cd`'d into a dependency checkout while exploring
# source and never returned before writing outputs/*.
RESCUE_MARKER="$(start_output_rescue_marker)"

# ── git push guard (mechanical, dmtools-agents#542) ─────────────────────────
# Interpose a `git` shim at the front of PATH for the WHOLE agent subprocess
# tree: the provider CLI (fa/claude/cursor/…) inherits it, so the LLM agent's
# own shell-tool `git push` is intercepted, and the JS post-actions' pushes
# (via cli_execute_command, PATH-resolved) go through it too. The shim
# refuses pushes to protected branches (main/master/default) and commit
# messages with closing keywords — prompts alone proved insufficient (the
# gh-992 incident: crafted "(closes #992)" commit pushed straight to main).
GIT_GUARD_DIR=""
if [ -f "${SCRIPT_DIR}/git-push-guard.sh" ]; then
  # Do not arm a second shim when one is already on PATH (the factory
  # workflow prepends its own guard dir for the whole step): two copies
  # would resolve each other as "real git" and exec-loop forever
  # (RCA 2026-09-28 legs hang). The shim itself also skips sibling…

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
  usage
  exit 1
fi

# --skip: print prompt and exit without running any agent (for post-action testing)
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ "$arg" = "--skip" ]; then
    PROMPT_FILE="${!#}"
    echo "=== --skip mode: printing prompt ==="
    echo ""
    cat "$PROMPT_FILE"
    echo ""
    echo "=== skipped agent execution ==="
    exit 0
  fi
done

# Load dmtools.env if exists (for local runs)
# `while IFS='=' read -r k v; ... export "${k}=${v}"` (matching
# run-teammate-local.sh's loader) instead of `source <(grep ...)`: `source`
# executes each line as a shell command, so any UNQUOTED value containing
# spaces (e.g. `JIRA_EXTRA_FIELDS=Acceptance criteria,Solution,...`) is
# parsed as `KEY=firstword secondword...` — a command invocation, not an
# assignment — which either errors ("command not found") or, worse, silently
# leaves that var (and, depending on shell/error-handling quirks, everything
# defined further down the file) unset. Splitting on the first '=' via `read`
# preserves the rest of the line — spaces included — as one literal value,
# with no shell re-evaluation.
if [ -f "dmtools.env" ]; then
  echo "Loading environment from dmtools.env"
  while IFS='=' read -r k v; do
    [[ "${k}" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]] || continue
    export "${k}=${v}"
  done < <(grep -E '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=' dmtools.env)
fi

# Extract prompt (last argument).
# When cliPrompt is used, DMTools passes the prompt as a temp file path — read it if so.
PROMPT_ARG="${!#}"
PROMPT_SOURCE="inline-argument"

if [ -f "$PROMPT_ARG" ]; then
  PROMPT="$(cat "$PROMPT_ARG")"
  PROMPT_SOURCE="$PROMPT_ARG"
else
  PROMPT="$PROMPT_ARG"
fi

if [ -z "$PROMPT" ]; then
  echo "Error: prompt argument is required" >&2
  usage
  exit 1
fi

PROMPT_BYTES=$(printf "%s" "$PROMPT" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
echo "=== AGENT PROMPT START ==="
echo "Prompt source: ${PROMPT_SOURCE}"
echo "Prompt size: ${PROMPT_BYTES} bytes"
echo ""
printf "%s\n" "$PROMPT"
echo ""
echo "=== AGENT PROMPT END ==="
echo ""

# Extract extra arguments (everything except the last — the prompt)
# These are passed through to the agent to support flags like --continue --resume
PASS_ARGS=()
if [ $# -gt 1 ]; then

fi

# Determine provider
PROVIDER="${AI_AGENT_PROVIDER:-cursor}"
echo "AI Agent Provider: $PROVIDER"

# Derive a human-readable usage name for token-report files.
# Prefer the agent config name (e.g. story_acceptance_criteria from CONFIG_FILE),
# then fall back to the workflow-provided AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE,
# and finally fall back to the provider name for standalone/local runs.
AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="${PROVIDER}"
CONFIG_FILE="${CONFIG_FILE:-${AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE:-}}"
if [ -n "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" ]; then
  case "${CONFIG_FILE}" in
    */.dmtools/packs/*)

      # agent pack (~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<v>/…, e.g. launch.json) —
      # report usage under the AGENT NAME (the pack dir), not the file
      # basename, so token-usage reports stay stable across the migration.
      usage_name="${CONFIG_FILE#*/.dmtools/packs/}"
      usage_name="${usage_name%%/*}"
      usage_name="${usage_name%-[0-9]*}"
      AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="${usage_name:-launch}"
      ;;
    *)
      AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="$(basename "${CONFIG_FILE}" .json)"
      ;;
  esac
fi
export AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME
echo "AI Agent Usage Name: ${AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME}"

## RCA

**Bug**: A dev leg that finishes its edits but whose verification (background job) hangs never writes `outputs/response.md`; the dev post-action's missing-response.md branch cold-resets the session (interrupted comment + Ready For Development + wip removal + red run via `throwInterruptedReset`), discarding a finished session's work and forcing a full re-run.

**Root cause**: 
1. `prompts/bash_tools.md` BGJOBS subgraph (B1–B6) gives no disposal rule for a HUNG background job — the agent has no guidance to stop a hung child and finish the deliverable (gh-1341: the agent parked 20:00–20:04 in a foreground sleep-poll circle, then the run died at the reset).
2. `js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js` response.md-missing branch immediately runs the cold-reset sequence — no cheaper recovery (resume of the still-resumable fa session) is attempted first.

**Fix approach**:
- C1: Add node B7 to the BGJOBS subgraph: hung job disposal rule.
- C2: In the missing-response.md branch of `developTicketAndCreatePR.js`, before the cold reset: if the fatal CLI/env class doesn't apply and the session is resumable, make exactly ONE bounded resume attempt via the wrapper (`bash agents/scripts/run-agent.sh --continue <prompt>`), then re-check response.md. #!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# ── Ensure Node/npm/npx are on PATH even in non-interactive shells ───────────
# Several providers below shell out to `npx @github/copilot@...`/`npx
# @anthropic-ai/claude-code` etc. when the CLI binary itself isn't globally
# installed. Node is typically managed by nvm, and nvm only auto-loads via
# ~/.bashrc — but ~/.bashrc's very first lines ("If not running
# interactively, don't do anything") make it a no-op for any NON-interactive
# shell, including `bash -lc "..."` (which is exactly how dmtools/Java spawns
# this script via ProcessBuilder, and how run-teammate-local.sh/CI invoke it
# too). Without this, every `npx ...` call fails outright with
# "npx: command not found" (exit 127) — but the surrounding Teammate job
# still reports success and its postJSAction still advances the ticket
# (labels + status change), producing a "completed" run that silently wrote
# NO content at all (see e.g. agents/js/assignForSolutionArchitecture.js).
# Guarded on `command -v npx` so this is a fast no-op once Node is already
# resolvable (global install, PATH already exporting nvm's bin dir, etc).
if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    \. "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" --no-use
    nvm use default >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm use node >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
fi

# Load shared helpers and provider implementations.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/_common.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/claude.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/codemie.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/copilot.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/fa.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/kimi.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/providers/cursor.sh"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") "prompt"

Runs the configured AI agent with the provided prompt.
Provider is controlled by AI_AGENT_PROVIDER environment variable (default: cursor).

Providers:
  cursor       - Uses cursor-agent (default)
  claude-code  - Uses Claude Code CLI via Bedrock proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  codemie      - Uses codemie-claude
  copilot      - Uses GitHub Copilot CLI (npx @github/copilot)
  fa           - Uses the Fa CLI (fa); requires FA_PROVIDER_TYPE +
                 FA_PROVIDER_MODEL, optional FA_PROVIDER_BASE_URL and
                 FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY
  kimi         - Uses Kimi Code CLI (kimi)

Example:
  $(basename "$0") "process the input folder"

Notes:
  - Provide the prompt as a single argument
  - Extra arguments before the prompt are passed through to the agent (cursor and codemie)
  - Useful for resume: $(basename "$0") --continue "fix the push error"
    (do NOT combine with --resume: Copilot CLI rejects --continue + --resume together)
  - For codemie: requires CODEMIE_API_KEY and CODEMIE_BASE_URL environment variables
  - For copilot: requires COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
  - For cursor: optional CURSOR_MODEL env var (default: auto)
  - For kimi: requires KIMI_API_KEY environment variable unless authenticated via OAuth;
              optional KIMI_BASE_URL and KIMI_MODEL
  - Final response is written to outputs/response.md
EOF
}

if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
  usage
  exit 1
fi

# --skip: print prompt and exit without running any agent (for post-action testing)
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ "$arg" = "--skip" ]; then
    PROMPT_FILE="${!#}"
    echo "=== --skip mode: printing prompt ==="
    echo ""
    cat "$PROMPT_FILE"
    echo ""
    echo "=== skipped agent execution ==="
    exit 0
  fi
done

# Load dmtools.env if exists (for local runs)
# `while IFS='=' read -r k v; ... export "${k}=${v}"` (matching
# run-teammate-local.sh's loader) instead of `source <(grep ...)`: `source`
# executes each line as a shell command, so any UNQUOTED value containing
# spaces (e.g. `JIRA_EXTRA_FIELDS=Acceptance criteria,Solution,...`) is
# parsed as `KEY=firstword secondword...` — a command invocation, not an
# assignment — which either errors ("command not found") or, worse, silently
# leaves that var (and, depending on shell/error-handling quirks, everything
# defined further down the file) unset. Splitting on the first '=' via `read`
# preserves the rest of the line — spaces included — as one literal value,
# with no shell re-evaluation.
if [ -f "dmtools.env" ]; then
  echo "Loading environment from dmtools.env"
  while IFS='=' read -r k v; do
    [[ "${k}" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]] || continue
    export "${k}=${v}"
  done < <(grep -E '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=' dmtools.env)
fi

# Extract prompt (last argument).
# When cliPrompt is used, DMTools passes the prompt as a temp file path — read it if so.
PROMPT_ARG="${!#}"
PROMPT_SOURCE="inline-argument"

if [ -f "$PROMPT_ARG" ]; then
  PROMPT="$(cat "$PROMPT_ARG")"
  PROMPT_SOURCE="$PROMPT_ARG"
else
  PROMPT="$PROMPT_ARG"
fi

if [ -z "$PROMPT" ]; then
  echo "Error: prompt argument is required" >&2
  usage
  exit 1
fi

PROMPT_BYTES=$(printf "%s" "$PROMPT" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
echo "=== AGENT PROMPT START ==="
echo "Prompt source: ${PROMPT_SOURCE}"
echo "Prompt size: ${PROMPT_BYTES} bytes"
echo ""
printf "%s\n" "$PROMPT"
echo ""
echo "=== AGENT PROMPT END ==="
echo ""

# Extract extra arguments (everything except the last — the prompt)
# These are passed through to the agent to support flags like --continue --resume
PASS_ARGS=()
if [ $# -gt 1 ]; then
  PASS_ARGS=("${@:1:$#-1}")
fi

# Determine provider
PROVIDER="${AI_AGENT_PROVIDER:-cursor}"
echo "AI Agent Provider: $PROVIDER"

# Derive a human-readable usage name for token-report files.
# Prefer the agent config name (e.g. story_acceptance_criteria from CONFIG_FILE),
# then fall back to the workflow-provided AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE,
# and finally fall back to the provider name for standalone/local runs.
AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="${PROVIDER}"
CONFIG_FILE="${CONFIG_FILE:-${AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE:-}}"
if [ -n "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" ]; then
  case "${CONFIG_FILE}" in
    */.dmtools/packs/*)
      # Pack launch surface (Wave 2): the config lives inside an unpacked
      # agent pack (~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<v>/…, e.g. launch.json) —
      # report usage under the AGENT NAME (the pack dir), not the file
      # basename, so token-usage reports stay stable across the migration.
      usage_name="${CONFIG_FILE#*/.dmtools/packs/}"
      usage_name="${usage_name%%/*}"
      usage_name="${usage_name%-[0-9]*}"
      AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="${usage_name:-launch}"
      ;;
    *)
      AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME="$(basename "${CONFIG_FILE}" .json)"
      ;;
  esac
fi
export AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME
echo "AI Agent Usage Name: ${AI_AGENT_USAGE_NAME}"

# Marker used by rescue_misplaced_outputs() (see providers/_common.sh) to
# detect output files the agent wrote to the wrong directory — e.g. because
# its persistent Bash shell `cd`'d into a dependency checkout while exploring
# source and never returned before writing outputs/*.
RESCUE_MARKER="$(start_output_rescue_marker)"

# ── git push guard (mechanical, dmtools-agents#542) ─────────────────────────
# Interpose a `git` shim at the front of PATH for the WHOLE agent subprocess
# tree: the provider CLI (fa/claude/cursor/…) inherits it, so the LLM agent's
# own shell-tool `git push` is intercepted, and the JS post-actions' pushes
# (via cli_execute_command, PATH-resolved) go through it too. The shim
# refuses pushes to protected branches (main/master/default) and commit
# messages with closing keywords — prompts alone proved insufficient (the
# gh-992 incident: crafted "(closes #992)" commit pushed straight to main).
GIT_GUARD_DIR=""
if [ -f "${SCRIPT_DIR}/git-push-guard.sh" ]; then
  # Do not arm a second shim when one is already on PATH (the factory
  # workflow prepends its own guard dir for the whole step): two copies
  # would resolve each other as "real git" and exec-loop forever
  # (RCA 2026-09-28 legs hang). The shim itself also skips sibling…
